meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'rent / lease' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: С другой стороны, можно просто в аренду сдавать.
examples.trans: On the other hand, we could simply rent it out.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть аренда.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always rent.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: instrumental of вечер used as an adverb

examples.trans: Come in the evening.
I'm at home in the evening.
Well, come in the evening.

meanings.note: Used for women too. Common masculine noun meaning 'doctor' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I need a doctor.
She's a doctor.

examples.text: Она там взятки для врачей хранит.
examples.trans: She keeps bribes for the doctors in there.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: Good afternoon!
I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Contrast дома = at home. Core Russian adv meaning '(to) home, homeward' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: And you go home and do your homework.
It's time to go home.

examples.text: Так, мы идём к слепым. А ты иди домой и делай уроки.
examples.trans: Right, we're going to the blind people. And you go home and do your homework.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'wife' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is my wife.
I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.
We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.en: to finish, to end, to complete
meanings.note: + acc. or infinitive. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'кончить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to finish, to complete', paired with 'заканчивать'.

examples.trans: I want to finish what I started.
When will you finish work?

examples.text: Был неправ. Простите. Я хочу закончить начатое.
examples.trans: I was wrong. Forgive me. I want to finish what I started.

meanings.note: A door, a shop, or a legal case. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.trans: We will close your case.
Close the door, please.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.en: in advance, beforehand, ahead of time
meanings.note: Temporal adverb.

examples.trans: Did you set all this up in advance?

examples.text: Мы купили билеты на поезд заранее.
examples.trans: We bought the train tickets in advance.

examples.text: Тогда заранее желаю вам приятного аппетита!
examples.trans: Then in advance I wish you bon appétit!

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Or even better.
Tea or coffee?
Or even better: a spa!

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When?
When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Чн is pronounced шн. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Of course I'll help.
Yes, of course.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: ложный вызов = false alarm; ложный гипс = fake cast

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, зачем вам этот ложный гипс на руках?
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, why do you need those fake casts on your arms?
It was a false alarm.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'minute' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll be there in ten minutes.
Just a minute!

examples.text: Ладно, будь там. Через десять минут буду.
examples.trans: All right, stay there. I'll be there in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Asking permission. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
Can you smoke here?
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

нельзя.gloss: it is not allowed; one can't

meanings.note: The opposite of можно. Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').
Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'льзя').

examples.trans: Not allowed? All right.
You can't smoke here.
Not allowed? All right, I'll go and do my homework.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is arranged'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и обговариваться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and is arranged on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют обговариваться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to is arranged.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Reflexive verb. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, find oneself', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'celebrate, mark'.

examples.text: Я не буду отмечать день рождения.
examples.trans: I will not celebrate my birthday.

examples.text: Я в этом году не буду шумно отмечать день рождения.
examples.trans: This year I will not noisily celebrate my birthday.

examples.text: Вся команда кухни собралась вечером отмечать общую победу.
examples.trans: The whole kitchen team gathered in the evening to celebrate their shared victory.

meanings.note: A prisoner, a hand. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пустить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let go, to release', paired with 'отпускать'.

Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'пустить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to let go, to release', paired with 'отпускать'.

examples.trans: Release him immediately!
Let me go home.
What bribe? Release him immediately!

meanings.en: to have a talk, to speak (with someone)
meanings.note: Поговорить с + instrumental. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: Talk to him.
We need to talk.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: Подожди! = wait!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to wait (a while)', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.trans: Wait, I'll be right there.
Wait a minute.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

meanings.note: + dative: 'позвони мне' = call me. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone', paired with 'звонить'.

examples.trans: Call me this evening.
I'll call tomorrow.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Asks about the reason.

examples.trans: Why are we going so slowly?
Why are you here?

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.en: to talk, to speak, to have a conversation
meanings.note: Prefix 'раз-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'говаривать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to talk, to speak'.

examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?
We're talking.

examples.text: А что вы так грубо разговариваете?
examples.trans: Why are you talking so rudely?

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'maternity hospital' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: В моём районе есть один неплохой роддом.
examples.trans: In my neighborhood there is a pretty good maternity hospital.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть роддом.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always maternity hospital.

meanings.note: День рождения = birthday. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'birth' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is his birthday today!
Happy birthday!

examples.text: Смотрите, врунишка новую машину купил! У врунишки сегодня день рождения!
examples.trans: Look, the little liar bought a new car! It's the little liar's birthday today!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: The г sounds like в.

examples.trans: I'm at home today.
I'll be there tonight.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'private event service' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я хочу закрыть ресторан на спецобслуживание.
examples.trans: I want to close the restaurant for a private event.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть спецобслуживание.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always private event service.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'contractions' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ой, Костя, кажется, у меня сейчас схватки начались!
examples.trans: Oh, Kostya, I think my contractions have just started!

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть схватка.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always contractions.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'contractions' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The morning contractions turned out to be false.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть схватки.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always contractions.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('morning').

examples.trans: A morning shift.
Our morning shift is starting soon.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('good, nice').

examples.trans: A good day.
What a lovely morning!

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'young man' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Young man, wait until we finish.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть юноша.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always young man.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
